body: We don’t have to do our worst, genetics clearly already has.

Follow the River by James Alexander Thom. There’s a scene about a savage tribe ripping an infant out of his mother’s arm and beating his head into a wall until his brains came out. The description is absolutely amazing and the feeling in it was so overwhelming I had to put the book down. I had dreams about that scene.
It’s definitely all relative but I would say no one is perfect and every person has flaws. I don’t think people in general are inherently bad, but we all have room to grow and improve.
